expect.note: GET /version answers {"sha": <7-40 lowercase hex> | null, "source": "image" | "unavailable" | "malformed"} and nothing else. The sha comes from a file baked into the image at build time and from nowhere else: with that file absent, empty or blank it reports sha null / source unavailable, and it does NOT fall back to the local git checkout -- which is what the `absent` probe grades, non-vacuously, because `git rev-parse HEAD` resolves where this suite runs, so a fallback would answer a real sha of a tree that is not the build. A file that holds something which is not a git sha -- a branch name, an unexpanded $ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, 6 hex, 41 hex, uppercase, a sha with a prefix or a suffix -- reports sha null / source malformed. Only a whole-string 7-40 lowercase hex value is echoed, with source `image`. Every probe runs with BUILD_SHA, ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA and VERSION set to a well-formed sha the file does not contain, so "it reads no environment variable" is graded rather than asserted.

provenance:
M44-P1, written before the route existed. M44's acceptance requires publishing the build sha of our own deploy (tasks/TODO.md M44; postmortem section 2's rule that a live-declared row is a claim about one deployed build), and the deployment could not report one: /version was 404, /healthz answers only {"ok": true}, and nothing in the repo carried a build identity -- the ceiling .github/workflows/deploy-smoke.yml has stated in a comment since M5 ("the app exposes no /version").

RED, twice, on two different mechanisms. First against no route at all: eight probes, every one of them a 404. Then the case was widened by a cold review and re-watched red against the FIRST implementation, which read an environment variable -- 10 of the 13 probes red, the three that stayed green being exactly the ones an env-reading route answers the same way (`absent`/`empty`/`whitespace` -> unavailable). That second red is the one worth recording, because the review's finding was not that the env route was wrong on any probe it had: it was that a platform service variable SHADOWS an image `ENV` at runtime, so a `BUILD_SHA` set by hand once outlives the deploy it was true for and the route cannot tell it from a baked one -- a confident lie with a hand-set knob to produce it. The file cannot be shadowed, so the knob is gone (ADR-033 Decision 2).

The probe set is chosen for the ways this goes WRONG rather than the way it goes right, because the failure this route exists to prevent is a confident wrong answer, not a missing one: 8 of 13 assert a null. Four groups, and three of them were added by that same cold review after it demonstrated that the original eight graded WHICH CHARACTERS are rejected and never the whole-string property, the case, or either bound -- so `re.match`, `re.search` and `re.IGNORECASE` all passed eight-for-eight. Each of the three is now watched red against a deliberately weakened matcher: `re.match` publishes `<40-hex>-dirty` and a 41-hex string whole; `re.search` publishes `release-<40-hex>` as well; `re.IGNORECASE` publishes the uppercase spelling. All three answer `source: "image"` while doing it, which is what makes them worse than a 404.

The `absent` probe's git-fallback conjunct was watched red the same way, by giving the route a `git rev-parse HEAD` fallback for the empty case: it answered {"sha": "fd3ae2aa77251d3bce4d91ecb18e003089e253af", "source": "image"} -- this worktree's HEAD, a real sha of a tree that produced no build. Its non-vacuity precondition was watched red too, by making `subprocess.run` raise: {"head-does-not-resolve": ...}. The precondition is that HEAD RESOLVES and not that a `.git` path exists, because a dangling worktree pointer satisfies `.exists()` and would have left the strongest probe in this set vacuous while reporting itself satisfied.

RED a third time, at PR #65 round 1 (R2), on a claim rather than on a behaviour. ADR-033's load-bearing sentence -- "it never reads an environment variable", the whole reason the design moved off ENV -- was asserted in three documents and graded by nothing: swapping build_identity for a version that falls back to os.environ['BUILD_SHA'] when the file is blank returned {'passed': True, 'wrong': {}}, because no probe ever set an environment variable and the fallback therefore never fired. The fix is the git fallback's lesson arrived at from the other end -- a negative claim is graded only where the eval SUPPLIES what the forbidden path would read -- so all thirteen probes now run with BUILD_SHA, ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA and VERSION set to a sha no probe writes to the file. The same mutation is now red on absent/empty/whitespace plus a named `env-fallback` conjunct: {'sha': 'beef1234...', 'source': 'image'}, a value the build never wrote.

triage.note:
Grades the ROUTE over HTTP, not just the helper, on the wall-clock ruling that a rule nothing consults is a comment (the reason `fast-wall-clock-budget` drives `evals.run.main()`). Loopback only -- no browser, no network, no spend -- which is what `invariant` admits; the case is `invariant`-only because the `fast` band cannot pay for another case (ADR-033 Decision 4).

Four declared ceilings. (1) A value that is genuinely 7-40 lowercase hex but is NOT a commit -- a 24-hex deployment id copied out of a dashboard, a date like `20260827`, a decimal build number -- is echoed as a sha, and nothing here or in the route can catch it: it is indistinguishable from an abbreviated sha without asking git, and asking git is the thing the route refuses to do. (2) It proves the two forbidden reads -- git at request time, and any environment variable -- by BEHAVIOUR, by supplying what each would read; it does not scan server.py for either. An implementation that consulted git or the environment only when the file was PRESENT AND VALID would pass, though it would have nothing to gain. (3) The precondition needs a resolvable HEAD, so a `container:` CI job, a `git archive` tarball or an installed copy reddens a suite gated at 100% with a correct route -- CI uses `actions/checkout`, which is the only environment where this has been checked. Tracked as `M44-P1-D2` (PR #65 R4), with the reviewer's ruling on the shape of the fix if it ever bites. (4) It says nothing about whether the sha the DEPLOYMENT reports is the sha it was built from: that is a property of the Dockerfile and of what Zeabur passes to a build, and only a live read of the deployed /version against the merge commit settles it (M44-P1's post-merge acceptance; ADR-033 Consequences).

It swaps `server.BUILD_SHA_FILE` for a temp path and restores it in a `finally`. That attribute has exactly one reader, which matters because `server` also runs background gateway tasks in this process -- the earlier env-var version mutated `os.environ`, which any future reader on a background path would have seen. A fifth, added with the environment fixture: the three names it sets are the plausible ones, not all of them. A route reading some fourth name -- `GIT_COMMIT`, `SOURCE_VERSION` -- is invisible here, the same bounded ceiling the git conjunct has against a second VCS.
